chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: How the Hoagy Carmichael album came about at the Riverboat
summary: Bob Wilber and Bill Borden, who had known Claude Thornhill, heard her at the Riverboat and used her on the album.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Okay, so you made your first record with the Worlds Greatest Jazz Band in 1969?

Well, no, while I was at the River Boat Bob Wilber - it was made in '69 but it wasn't, although there were members of the Worlds Greatest Jazz Band in the group it was under Bob Wilber's label. Bob came in . . .
Under Bob Wilber's name. The music of Hoagy Carmichael.
Bob came in and said that he was making this album of the music of Hoagy Carmichael
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

and that he had spoken to Bill Gordon of Monmouth-Evergreen Records about a vocal because it doesn't make sense to have an Hoagy Carmichael album and not have vocals. So Bill Borden said, well where are you going to find a singer around, you know, that can do it. So Bob recommended me. And so Bill Borden came down to the River Boat and he heard me while I was there and he agreed. He said, yeah, fine, if you'll do this then after this comes out you can do an album with selections of your own choice. So we made the album on the music of Hoagy Carmichael and I did four selections, "Skylark", "Georgia On My Mind", "In the Cool Cool Cool Of The Evening", and "I Get Along Without You Very Well".
Five. Anyway it turned out that Bill Borden had been associated with Claude Thornhill in the past but it was . . .
Yeah, yeah, he played trumpet with the band.

So he really didn't know me. So after we did the Music Of Hoagy Carmichael then I did the album Closest Pages In A Book, and I used a small combination under the direction of Bob Wilber. And then I made another album Monmouth-Evergreen with Dick Hyman. Dick Hyman had been on that earlier album, the Andy Razaff album along with some other little things I had done here and there. And Dick had, what can I say, composed some music to some Shakespear lyrics, just some stray little pieces. And Dick said because he had accompanied me at some time in the distant past that the first time he accompanied a singer he had me in mind when he decided to do this catalogue of Shakespear of songs. So he asked me to do them so I made the album with Dick. It's called Sullivan, Shakespear and Hyman. And so it's a little far-fetched. It's not what you would call a jazz recording but it has some nice little arrangements of the Shakespear things. We call it 'tongue-in-cheek, painless Shakespear'.
